Theme

Construction, trades & building materials

scaffold noun

also scaffolding

classical

Digest 13.6.5.7 (Ulpian): a plasterer lent out falls dē māchinā; the risk differs if he was lent to work dē plānō, on the ground, or if the scaffold was minus dīligenter … ligāta or failed through fūnium perticārumque vetustāte
Vitruvius 7.2.2: māchinīs comparātīs (scaffolds set up for vaulting rooms)
Vitruvius 10.1.1: scānsōriae māchinae, built tignīs statūtīs et trānsversāriīs conligātīs
M-O s.v. scaffolding

māchina, māchinae f.

noun, first declension

Scaffold or scaffolding for building, the Roman word. Lewis & Short I.B.3 also cites Pliny 19.2.8 §30 (NH 19.30), but there māchinīs aedificātiōnum means building machinery such as hoists, which is weak evidence for scaffolding. The noun is broader than modern English “machine.”

Other words

  • māchina ex fistulīs ferreīs — scaffolding made of iron tubes

    also used · our formation

    Our descriptive phrase for the modern construction-site object.

  • compāgēs, compāgis f. — framework

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. scaffolding

    Classically it never names a builder’s scaffold; the scaffolding sense is modern lexicographic (Morgan–Owens). Useful as a gloss word, not as the narrative noun.

  • pēgma, pēgmatis n. — framework, stage machinery

    noun, third declension · also used · classical

    Another ancient framework/machinery noun, especially for theatrical stage machinery and board fixtures. Its ancient examples do not by themselves establish the modern tube-and-clamp construction sense; māchina has the clearer explicit builder’s-scaffold entry.

Examples

  • Operārius in māchinā stat.

    The worker is standing on the scaffold.composed

  • Māchinam juxtā domum cōnstruunt.

    They are assembling the scaffolding beside the house.composed

  • Dē plānō lūde, nōn in māchinā.

    Play on the ground, not on the scaffold (after the Digest’s dē plānō).composed

See also upright, crossbar, scaffold pole, scaffold platform, framework, scaffold worker, assemble, dismantle.
